newsitem.title: UK: Annington Homes bonds expected by Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Annington Homes bonds expected by Wednesday.

text.p: Annington Homes -- the consortium that bought British Ministry of Defence living quarters -- will launch three bonds worth around 865 million stg by Wednesday, syndicate managers said on Monday.
HSBC Markets and Nomura International will be joint lead managers on the transaction which will securitise rental income from the properties.
The largest issue was expected to be a long-dated 360 million stg fixed-rate bond with a 20-year average life and priced in the low 30s basis points over gilts.
A 330 million stg FRN with a five-year average life was thought likely at around 1/16 point over LIBOR.
The third leg will be a 175 million stg fixed-rate bond with a 12.5 year average life and pricing in the low to mid-30s b.p. over gilts.

The transaction is considered a quasi-sovereign deal, as payments are secured by British government guarantees and all bonds will be rated AAA grade by Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp.
A syndicate official said demand was expected to come from British institutional investors.
The MoD sold 57,400 homes for 1.662 billion stg to Annington last month in a deal underwritten by Nomura International.
The Annington Homes consortium is made up of Abbey National Treasury Services, AMEC Group, Hambros Bank, Midland Bank, Nomura and the Royal Bank of Scotland.
The deal is part of the government's so-called private finance initiative, which aims to shift the capital cost -- and risk -- of public investments into private hands.
